items.title: MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash
items.summary:
MAI Cyber 2 Flash: Leading security. Lower cost
MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash: two new coding models built for the everyday enterprise coding tasks, delivering leading performance at a fraction of the cost of competing models.
MAI Code 2 is at the frontier of price-performance for common enterpris
items.text:
MAI Cyber 2 Flash: Leading security. Lower cost
MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash: two new coding models built for the everyday enterprise coding tasks, delivering leading performance at a fraction of the cost of competing models.
MAI Code 2 is at the frontier of price-performance for common enterprise coding tasks and excels in taking code to production, deep debugging, multi-file implementation, repo wide reasoning, and UI. It does all of this while also delivering changes code maintainers would merge, at a fraction of frontier cost.
Meanwhile, MAI Code 2 Flash is designed for high-volume work such as code explanations, targeted edits, routine fixes, and rapid iterations, while bringing quality at a much lower cost.
To deliver the best price-performance, we’ve built these models to prioritize the coding work our customers do every day. They’re explicitly not yet tuned for harder problems, like fundamental science research and very long horizon agentic work.
Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot (DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal Bench 2.1, SWE-Atlas and FrontierCode v1.1), MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at 40% of the cost, and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5’s performance at just 5% of the cost.1
MAI Code 2 is also tuned for producing great dashboards and visualizations, and excels at visual coding. In blind frontend app evaluations, reviewers preferred its results over GPT-6 Sol 64% of the time.2
In addition, MAI Code 2 Flash offers comparable performance to GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 at 65% and 20% of the cost, across three coding benchmarks measuring day-to-day, high-volume routine coding tasks.3
MAI Code 2 is also becoming the workhorse behind Microsoft products. From Code 2 Flash we further optimized a single model, MAI Work Flash, to serve multiple Microsoft products across M365 and Fabric IQ. 
Excel: Our model is on par for accuracy and token efficiency with GPT 6 Luna across key internal Excel customer-scenario benchmarks.
PowerPoint: On key production benchmark scenarios that measure frequent PowerPoint tasks, our model performs on par with GPT 6 Luna in both quality and token efficiency.
Word: Our model performs similar to GPT 6.1 sol (while being significantly smaller) on 5 key internal benchmarks using ~42% fewer input tokens per call than GPT6.1 Sol in production.
Teams: Our model beats GPT 6 Luna at tracking decisions, filling knowledge gaps, and adapting custom instructions using up to 28% fewer tokens on instruction following and tool calling.
FabricIQ: In offline evaluation runs our MAI model outperforms GPT-5.6-sol, GPT-6-astra, and Opus-5.5 at DAX query generation, the core capability behind “Chat with your Data” for Power BI semantic models.
Get started
MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash are available in GitHub Copilot, and Code 2 Flash is in limited-access preview in Microsoft Foundry. Soon, we’ll be releasing it on Open Router, Vercel, Hermes, Open Code, and Kilo.
Learn more about customizing MAI Code 2 on our Custom Models page.
About these results
Results reflect evaluations on specific coding tasks and configurations. Performance and cost comparisons vary by workload, model configuration, reasoning effort, and pricing assumptions.

Vitality Roses head coach Anna Stembridge has been hit by multiple injuries ahead of her side's upcoming Vitality Netball Horizon Series against Jamaica; Alicia Scholes will miss the remainder of the season, while Olivia Tchine and Sasha Glasgow will not make the series
Tuesday 17 November 2026 19:06, UK
Alicia Scholes has been ruled out of the remainder of the 2026 season after she suffered a ruptured ACL during a training camp with England's Vitality Roses.
England Netball say Scholes, who is the daughter of Manchester United great Paul Scholes, will commence her rehabilitation immediately and will be supported by both the governing body and London Pulse's medical and performance teams.
"We're all gutted for Alicia," Roses head coach Anna Stembridge said, as she unveiled her squads for her side's upcoming Vitality Netball Horizon Series on Tuesday.

"She's been working incredibly hard in camp, and it's been great to see her developing combinations and making her mark within the group.
"To have her season end this way is hugely disappointing, but she has the full support of both England Netball and London Pulse as she begins her rehabilitation."
Stembridge also announced Olivia Tchine and Sasha Glasgow had been omitted from both home and away squads for her side's upcoming Vitality Netball Horizon Series due to injury.
The series will see the Roses face Jamaica on November 21 and 22 in a two-match series at London's Copper Box Arena, before travelling to face the same opponent in the away leg in Kingston on December 5 and 6.
Nat Metcalf, Ella Clark and Berri Neal have all been drafted into the squad. Metcalf returns to the court after sustaining an injury at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.
Neal will act as a travelling reserve for both home and away legs, while Clark, who made her Commonwealth Games debut in the summer, will be included in the full squad for the opening match, before also moving to become a second travelling reserve for the second match.
Izzi Phillips, who had previously been a travelling reserve for the away leg, has been elevated to the squad for the full series.
Vice-captain Tchine suffered an injury in October and will miss the series as she completes her return-to-play protocols.
Glasgow had picked up her injury in training before coming into camp, and will miss the home leg of the series, before joining the squad in Jamaica for the final two matches.
Stembridge said: "It's never easy to lose players through injury, particularly at this stage of our preparations.
"Liv [Olivia Tchine] and Sasha [Glasgow] both need a little more time in their return-to-play journeys, and we'll continue to support them as they work towards getting back on court."
Reflecting on her injury, Tchine said: "I'm absolutely gutted to not be playing in the Vitality Netball Horizon Series this year.
"Just like every other England game, I was looking forward to playing against some of the world's best players. Injuries are annoying and frustrating but I'm working so hard to make sure that I'm back on court for the next series.

items.title: As decision model use skyrockets, is customization the next frontier?
items.summary:
In October, more than one in four requests on Vercel’s AI model router went to decision models, not LLMs — an enormous share of work for a kind of computerized intelligence that was invented only a month earlier.
Decision models are LLMs that don’t produce output tokens; instead, they’re tuned to us
items.text:
In October, more than one in four requests on Vercel’s AI model router went to decision models, not LLMs — an enormous share of work for a kind of computerized intelligence that was invented only a month earlier.
Decision models are LLMs that don’t produce output tokens; instead, they’re tuned to use their general intelligence to quickly and cheaply decide between preset options, while registering its level of confidence in the choice. They’re useful in production environments, where fast decisions can be more important than the reasoning provided by a slower and more expensive frontier model.
TypeSafe became a $7.5 billion company after releasing its Jev family of models, which continues to dominate usage (at least where we can see metrics from services like OpenRouter, which handled more than 1.5 billion queries to TypeSafe’s models last week).
However, it’s easy to make a decision model, and dozens were released in the wake of Jev. One Amazon engineer made one in a weekend, and soon every hyperscaler had its own option. On Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that his company is rolling out its decision model, Microsoft-Decision-1.1, for wide use on Azure immediately.
The action is happening on both ends of the ecosystem: Sqwish, a U.K.-based AI startup behind a decision model called kettei fat, announced a $3 million pre-seed round today. Co-founders Ushnish Sengupta and Federica Freddi, who met as Cambridge grad students, had been developing small LLMs when Jev arrived on the scene, and they realized their architectures could be repurposed as a powerful decision model.
Data appears to be the key to a successful model in this category — TypeSafe CEO Diogo Almeida told TechCrunch that the hardest part of building Jev was finely calibrating its judgement using statistically-adjusted synthetic data. Sqwish, too, has been working with synthetic data, but its unique offering is built-in post-training tools that use a customer’s own data to improve the model’s judgement.
“What makes us not a commodity, I think, is the fact that we are offering our customers the same power…they can keep uploading their production data, and just the same way that we trained our models, their models can also keep getting better at the tasks that they care about,” CEO Ushnish Sengupta told TechCrunch.
Attempting to rank decision models is difficult; Sqwish’s “kettei fat” model has performed well on some benchmarks, but most builders of the technology say that the real proof is in the pudding: It’s generally simple for developers to sub in one model for another and see how it does in a specific context.
“The benchmark is more of an invitation to try the model out, and then the continual tuning is the reason why they should stick to us,” Sengupta said.
The Microsoft-Decision-1.1 model is also the result of the company carefully balancing across cost, latency, intelligence and calibration. Achint Srivastava, the engineering VP who led the project, agreed that too much focus on benchmarks is a mistake.
“What we see is that ‘benchmaxed’ models fall flat under real enterprise usage very quickly,” Srivastava wrote in an email. “Our testing underscores just how challenging it is to deliver accuracy, reliability, speed and cost efficiency in a single model. Microsoft-Decision-1.1 and Jev are among the few that perform strongly across all four dimensions, even when evaluated on ‘held out’ or unseen benchmarks reflective of real use cases.”
For startups like Sqwish, competition with hyperscalers and frontier labs is an opportunity. Freddi predicts that future systems will see so-called System One intelligence, like decision models, working in concert with System Two intelligence, like frontier LLMs.
“Even in that future, System One is maybe a $10 billion, $50 billion [opportunity], and OpenAI is doing this IPO with you know $1 trillion, $2 trillion market value in mind,” she told TechCrunch. “This is all we care about; whereas for them, this is just a side project.”

items.title: Pedestal AI raises $4.7 million to agentify the supply chain
items.summary:
Delivery supply chains are the lifeblood of contemporary businesses — and a new startup is betting that purpose-built AI agents can make them run a lot more smoothly.
On Tuesday, Pedestal AI emerged from stealth with $4.7 million in seed funding. The company’s goal is to use agentic AI to make suppl
items.text:
Delivery supply chains are the lifeblood of contemporary businesses — and a new startup is betting that purpose-built AI agents can make them run a lot more smoothly.
On Tuesday, Pedestal AI emerged from stealth with $4.7 million in seed funding. The company’s goal is to use agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable — a plan that’s already brought them together with Fortune 500 companies and some of the largest shipping firms in the world.
The seed round was led by Eclipse, with participation from RRE, Converge VC, Timescale VC and VitalStage. Pedestal says the funding will be used to expand its product and engineering time, grow the marketing organization, and support additional deployments.
In practice, much of Pedestal’s work is about removing friction from the shipping process — with agentic technology used as a means to that end. In one case, the company reduced missed deliveries for a major furniture company by 20% by deploying agents to take on some of the work that drivers were supposed to do. The agentic system they built would call customers 30 minutes before a delivery and collect any special instructions; if the call didn’t go through, a text would be sent from a separate system. Along the way, the deployment collected a wealth of data about friction points in the process, which could be used to optimize the system even further.
CEO Raj Aggarwal says contemporary AI systems are particularly useful for dealing with that data. “The challenge is that the data is messy and it’s constantly changing,” Aggarwal told TechCrunch. “It’s disparate because it sits in so many legacy systems. That’s what makes it hard.”
Supply chain AI has become a particularly hot space in recent months as alumni from autonomous driving teams look to launch their own startups. The supply chain startup Atomic, launched by a team of Tesla alumni, came out of stealth in 2025 with an emphasis on streamlining inventory. Another venture called Loop was launched by Uber alums to focus on predictive analytics.
As Aggarwal sees it, deliveries are particularly well-suited to training reinforcement learning systems. Because of their high volumes and easily measured outcomes, it’s easy to fine-tune contemporary AI systems towards what’s working and away from what isn’t.
Perhaps most importantly, it’s the kind of problem that can have an immediate effect on a client’s bottom line, making it easy to justify the expense.
“If you can get it right,” he told TechCrunch, “you can have really big impact.”

items.text:
Arsenal Double winner Storey dies aged 81
- Published
Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey has died at the age of 81.
Storey made 501 appearances in all competitions for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, scoring 17 goals.
He was part of the Double-winning Arsenal team which secured the First Division title and FA Cup in 1970-71 under manager Bertie Mee.
"Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of double winner Peter Storey," Arsenal said in a statement.
"All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.
"We will pay our respects to Peter at our forthcoming home match against Borussia Dortmund."
Surrey-born Storey joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 and made his first-team debut against Leicester City in 1965, initially starting his career at right-back before being moved into midfield.
He is currently eighth on Arsenal's list of all-time appearance holders and was capped 19 times by England, although he did not feature in a major tournament for the Three Lions.
Storey collected runners-up medals with Arsenal in the League Cup in 1967-68 and 1968-69 and in the FA Cup in 1971-72.
He joined Second Division Fulham on a free transfer in March 1977 and made 19 appearances for the Cottagers before his contract was terminated later that year and he retired.
However, Storey had something of a troubled life after his retirement from professional football.
He was convicted of running a brothel - for which he received a suspended prison sentence in 1979 - and was later jailed for three years for his involvement in a counterfeiting operation, then served another prison sentence in 1990 for attempting to smuggle pornographic videos into Britain.

items.title: Proton’s Lumo, a privacy-focused alternative to ChatGPT and Claude, arrives on desktop
items.summary: Proton, the privacy-focused tech company offering alternatives to Google and Microsoft’s tools for email, productivity apps, password management, cloud storage, and more, is now bringing its AI app Lumo to personal computers. On Tuesday, the company launched Lumo Desktop for Windows, macOS, and Linu
items.text:
Proton, the privacy-focused tech company offering alternatives to Google and Microsoft’s tools for email, productivity apps, password management, cloud storage, and more, is now bringing its AI app Lumo to personal computers. On Tuesday, the company launched Lumo Desktop for Windows, macOS, and Linux, allowing users to leverage its AI to carry out local tasks on their computer involving connected apps, personal files, and other automations.
The app is designed to offer users more control over their personal data, as consumer AI technology becomes focused more on AI agents that can perform tasks on users’ behalf, rather than just answering questions.
Already, the major model makers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and others, offer desktop tools for working with their AI technologies, but doing so invites increased risk to users’ personal data. Only this week, for instance, Apple announced it was addressing those privacy concerns with tightened security settings for apps that request Full Disk Access, as the AI desktop apps do.
Proton’s idea is to offer a set of tools that let its AI access connected apps, files, and folders and automate tasks, but with more personalization over how much access the AI has. The company says users can choose which actions the AI agent takes that will need to request their approval, and it vows that the conversations and information from connected apps and files are never used to serve personalized ads or train AI models.
The new app includes a variety of connectors that support local tools, like file-system access, shell execution, and browser content fetching; plus, Proton’s email app and other third-party services including Confluence, Dropbox, and Jira.
The connectors also support local and remote MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, which AI agents use to access external data sources.
Proton says that users can decide for each connector which actions Lumo can perform automatically, which require approval, and which are blocked entirely. Users can also turn individual tools off from the Tools menu in their conversation.
In addition, users can set up their own scheduled tasks, where each has its own set of permissions, in terms of what can be handled automatically and what requires approval.
Proton notes that it uses encryption to ensure that only users can read their chat history, not the company. The company also says it keeps no server-side logs, and the limited data it does store is protected under Swiss privacy law. The data is hosted on European infrastructure, outside the scope of the U.S. CLOUD Act, which specifies how law enforcement agencies access data held by cloud service providers.
The company says it’s investing in its infrastructure, with its first NVIDIA B300 cluster built on Open Compute Project (OCP) standards now going live in Switzerland.
Similar to other AI apps, Lumo’s desktop app supports Skills, which let users save instructions, templates, and reference files that Lumo can reuse across their conversations. (An earlier version of this, Custom Lumos, will now be migrated to the Skills format.)

items.title: AI models can be tricked into identifying civilians as military targets by telling them it’s a game
items.summary:
Some AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other leading AI labs could be easily tricked into identifying targets for military strikes — even if they include civilians or locations like schools — simply by being told they’re playing a game, according to a new research report by Vals.
Vals, a San Fra
items.text:
Some AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other leading AI labs could be easily tricked into identifying targets for military strikes — even if they include civilians or locations like schools — simply by being told they’re playing a game, according to a new research report by Vals.
Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. Researchers used simulated scenarios and a combination of generated and real imagery from Ukraine and Iran to see if the AI models would mark targets in drone and satellite imagery.
The models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, and other companies frequently identified potential targets in drone and satellite imagery, including civilians and surrendering soldiers. When the models refused to cooperate, researchers were able to jailbreak them by claiming the battlefield scenarios were part of a game.
The findings come amid growing fears about the immediate risks posed by AI, beyond the existential threats associated with artificial general intelligence.
Earlier this year, Anthropic became embroiled in a dispute with the Department of Defense after it told the agency it could not use Anthropic’s technology for mass surveillance of Americans or autonomous warfare. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has insisted that today’s AI systems aren’t reliable enough to make life-or-death decisions without a human in the loop. Meanwhile, the Pentagon argued it should be able to deploy the technology for any lawful military purpose.
The new research raises further questions about whether AI companies are capable of preventing their models from being used in warfare.
Ironically, AI models from Anthropic performed the worst in these simulated scenarios. But none of the models performed particularly well. None of the researchers’ requests were blocked by a safety classifier, and refusals were uncommon. Even when models did refuse, they often complied after being told they were playing a game.
Anthropic spokesperson Eduardo Maia Silva told TechCrunch the company appreciates Vals’s report, recommendations, and collaboration, and acknowledged that the outcomes were not acceptable.
“The examples in the report are very clearly against our rules and we have banned and will ban users when we see this behavior,” according to an emailed company statement sent by Silva. “Even for authorized settings, Anthropic has long been firm that today’s frontier AI systems are not reliable enough to power fully autonomous weapons.”
Anthropic told TechCrunch that its teams were already developing additional safeguards before the report was published and that those measures would be in place soon. Anthropic is also expanding its own testing and enhancing safeguards and enforcement to address any gaps it finds.
OpenAI spokesperson Nate Evans told TechCrunch the company prohibits using its public models to facilitate violence or for unapproved national security purposes, including in the scenarios Vals simulated.
“We actively detect and disrupt misuse, including by suspending accounts that violate our policies,” OpenAI said in an emailed statement. “We’re also developing additional safeguards for our public models against misuse involving drones and drone software.”
Vals notes in the report that the models were never asked to directly make strike decisions, a task the researchers said the models would typically refuse. That doesn’t mean their outputs couldn’t have dire or fatal consequences in the real world. For instance, targeting information could be used by autonomous weapons systems.
In some scenarios, the models were asked to report whether people were visible. Positive reports were followed by simulated strikes and the models would see the consequences.
The report relies on commercial models from frontier AI labs, not the models those companies might provide to the military. It’s not clear what the additional safeguards would apply to military use, though.
Vals also noted that technical challenges, including latency and limited onboard computing capacity, make it difficult to use general-purpose AI models for live drone targeting. Those constraints make their deployment in combat less of an immediate threat.
A more immediate threat, the researchers say, is that AI models could be used to annotate battlefield footage at scale, producing training data for autonomous targeting systems.
For instance, researchers relied on real satellite imagery of an Iranian school that was bombed by the U.S. in February 2026, killing more than 150 civilians. Bloomberg later reported that an “overreliance on AI” contributed to the strike. In Vals’s testing, models frequently marked the school, which sat next to a military complex, as a strike target, with Claude Opus 5.5 selecting the school in 69% of ordinary trials and 72% of game-framed trials.
Anthropic no longer has an active Pentagon contract, but other companies including SpaceXAI, OpenAI, and Google do. A recent Congressional Research Service report found that the Pentagon is not known to be using any frontier AI model directly in autonomous weapons systems directly.
TechCrunch has also reached out to Meta, Google, Thinking Machines Lab, and SpaceXAI for comment.

items.title: ‘I’m entering to win’: Philippe Diallo launches campaign to topple Gianni Infantino
items.summary:
Philippe Diallo, Europe’s candidate to fight Gianni Infantino for the Fifa presidency, said he had received “strong signs of support from other continents” as he launched his campaign in Paris on Tuesday.
The French Football Federation president also said he had contacted Kozo Tashima, who announced
items.text:
Philippe Diallo, Europe’s candidate to fight Gianni Infantino for the Fifa presidency, said he had received “strong signs of support from other continents” as he launched his campaign in Paris on Tuesday.
The French Football Federation president also said he had contacted Kozo Tashima, who announced his candidacy this month, and would try to convince him to “join forces”. Diallo did not indicate whether he would explicitly be asking Tashima to stand aside. “Our approaches are based on the same assessments and the same values,” he said.
Diallo revealed the first figure from Uefa to encourage him to mount a late challenge had been the Football Association chair, Debbie Hewitt. With strong European backing, the 63-year-old has secured 55 of the 106 votes needed to unseat Infantino, the favourite in March’s election.
“With the unanimous support of Uefa, I already have a large base of votes,” Diallo said. “It’s now up to me and my team to go and convince those on other continents. Since yesterday, I’ve had strong signs of support from other continents which will be revealed in the coming days.”
Diallo’s candidacy was ratified by the FFF’s executive committee on Tuesday, one day before the deadline to declare for the election. Tashima, the Japan FA’s honorary president, is the only other person to have said they will take on Infantino. “Initially I wasn’t running,” Diallo said, “but the insistence of my European colleagues, as well as others, led me to accept the proposal.”
Diallo has worked in French football since 1992, chairing the lobby group Union des Clubs Professionnels de Football for almost 30 years before joining the FFF in 2021. He was elected president two years later, having initially stepped up in an interim capacity.
 
He is also very familiar with the inner workings of Fifa, having been a judge in its dispute resolution chamber for more than two decades.
“I have the experience, the conviction and the values to make my candidacy a credible alternative to the current Fifa leadership,” he said. “I’m entering this campaign not just to provide a different voice, but to win. What has happened over the last few months has shocked the footballing world and does not match our vision for the future of football.”
Diallo, who formally withdrew the FFF’s support for Infantino in September, said he was “aware of the responsibility” of his candidacy: “I’m doing this to be in line with everything that we’ve been saying since this summer, and even before that.”
Diallo reiterated his criticism of Infantino and railed against what he described as “solitary governance” at Fifa. “The great issues of football are being decided behind the scenes, with no transparency, without consulting the stakeholders,” he said.
According to Diallo, recent events have “damaged football’s image, its credibility, and have introduced the poison of division”. He cited the Fifa Peace Prize, the lifting of Folarin Balogun’s red-card suspension during the World Cup, the extended half-time break during the final and the failed World Cup sell-off plan.
Diallo indicated he had not spoken with Infantino in months. “The last time I saw him was at the World Cup, when he came to a few France matches,” he said. “Unfortunately he didn’t take the opportunity to share some of his projects with us. I considered that to be an act of defiance.”
Diallo said he would go into detail on his manifesto on 6 December at the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in Belfast. “My vision is that of open governance,” he said. “It’s one where the authorities truly play their role and the president is in charge of vision and strategy but leaves the day-to-day management to the secretary general. I think that certain stakeholders, namely the clubs and players, need to be more directly involved.”

Last chance to vote for BBC Women's Footballer of the Year 2026
- Published
Voting for the BBC World Service Women's Footballer of the Year 2026 will close at 09:00 GMT on Wednesday, 18 November.
Fans worldwide can vote from the five-player shortlist of Temwa Chawinga, Ewa Pajor, Alexia Putellas, Alessia Russo and Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw.
For the first time in the award's history, the winner will be announced as part of the BBC's Sports Personality of the Year on Sunday, 13 December as well as on the BBC World Service and the BBC Sport website and app.
Contenders for the award - now in its 12th year - are nominated by coaches, journalists and former professionals. It covers the period September 2025-August 2026.
Cast your vote, and read more on the five contenders.
Temwa Chawinga
Age: 28 Country: Malawi
Club: Kansas City Position: Forward
Chawinga has established herself as one of the world's most prolific forwards.
Her impact on the National Women's Soccer League is clear. Her extraordinary form helped Kansas City Current clinch the NWSL Shield as the league's top team in the regular season.
Chawinga scored 15 goals in the 2025 season as she became the first player to be named NWSL MVP in back-to-back campaigns. She also won the Golden Boot for the second year in a row.
Those performances earned her a contract extension through until 2029.
Chawinga returned to international football with Malawi for the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations.
Alongside her sister Tabitha, she helped Malawi reach the country's first Wafcon final and - in doing so - qualify for the Women's World Cup for the first time.
Chawinga scored against Nigeria, Egypt, Ghana and Algeria at Wafcon, winning the tournament's Golden Boot with five goals.
Ewa Pajor
Age: 29 Country: Poland
Club: Barcelona Position: Forward
Pajor is widely regarded as a world-class number nine - and it's clear why.
Instrumental as Barcelona won four trophies last season, Pajor scored their first two goals in a 4-0 Champions League final victory over Lyon.
The goals meant she finished as the competition's top scorer, while the result meant she won the Champions League for the first time after losing in five finals - four with Wolfsburg and one with Barcelona.
Pajor also enjoyed an outstanding second season with Barcelona in Liga F, scoring 16 league goals in her 23 appearances and providing five assists. She was a key player as Barca won the domestic treble.
On the international stage, Pajor captains Poland and is the team's leading goalscorer.
Alexia Putellas
Age: 32 Country: Spain
Club: London City Lionesses Position: Midfielder
Putellas showed again this year why she is one of the most influential footballers in the world.
After 14 years with Barcelona, she delivered a spectacular final season with the club - helping them win four major trophies.
Her 14 goal contributions in 11 Champions League appearances helped her childhood club win the competition for the fourth time, and she remained a decisive figure bringing experience and leadership when it mattered most.
Putellas delayed announcing her move to London City Lionesses to avoid creating a distraction, but in July 2026 she completed that transfer, saying the club's "women-only identity and ambition" were important factors.
Internationally, Putellas was instrumental in Spain retaining the Women's Nations League in late 2025, scoring three goals against Sweden in the semi-finals before being named player of the finals as Spain defeated Germany 3–0.
Last month she was awarded a record-equalling third Ballon d'Or.
Alessia Russo
Age: 27 Country: England
Club: Arsenal Position: Forward
Russo has proven to once again be a trusted and integral attacking force for Arsenal, while remaining a key player for England.
She scored 13 WSL goals last season to finish second in the league's scoring charts, and also added six assists in her 22 appearances. In total, she registered 24 goals and eight assists across all competitions.
Among the highlights of her season was winning the inaugural Women's Champions Cup with Arsenal, beating Corinthians 3- 2 after extra time.
It was the first competitive trophy Arsenal's women's team had lifted at the Emirates, though they finished runners-up to Manchester City in the WSL.
Russo remains a first-choice striker for England and in April scored her 30th senior international goal to move into the top 10 of Lionesses goalscorers.
She was also nominated for the PFA Player of the Year award.
Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw
Age: 29 Country: Jamaica
Club: Manchester City Position: Forward
After a fine year, Shaw has positioned herself as one of the world's elite forwards.
The defining striker in Manchester City's Women Super League title-winning campaign, she scored 21 goals in 22 league appearances, won a record third consecutive WSL Golden Boot and was named WSL Player of the Season.
Her goals were central to City ending a 10-year wait for the league title.
They went on to complete the Double, with Shaw scoring the opening goal in their FA Cup final victory over Brighton at Wembley to finish the season with 26 goals in all competitions.
She also reached a major personal milestone in December 2025 when she became the first player in the history of City's professional women's team to score 100 goals.
Amid uncertainty over her future, Shaw announced at City's end-of-season celebrations that she had signed a new four-year contract through to 2030.
Who are the previous winners?
- Hannah Hampton (2025)
- Barbra Banda (2024)
- Mary Earps (2023)
- Beth Mead (2022)
- Vivianne Miedema (2021)
- Lucy Bronze (2020)
- Ada Hegerberg (2019)
- Lucy Bronze (2018)
- Ada Hegerberg (2017)
- Kim Little (2016)
- Asisat Oshoala (2015)

items.title: Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable
items.summary: The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club mana
items.text:
The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments.
There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching in to the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the 4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows.
Pocognoli’s team scored five goals in six Nations League games, four coming against North Macedonia. They drew blanks in three fixtures. The concession of 10 depicts a team soft against set pieces and open play. Scotland have wingers who are not appropriately deployed because of dedication to a system. They have an obvious shortage of centre-backs yet Pocognoli picks three at a time. The midfield lacks balance. Not one player under Pocognoli’s watch is consistently excelling.
Pocognoli is obstinate in respect of his tactics. At club level this can work owing to daily work on a training pitch. Scotland are wedded to a 3-4-2-1 that fits too few of their players. There is no transfer window capacity to change that. Pocognoli’s insistence upon his “philosophy” sets off alarm bells. Although his English is strong, it is far from perfect, which raises questions about communication. Scotland do not look well drilled or clear in approach, which was plain in the unimpressive home win against North Macedonia even before the Switzerland debacle.
There is no detailed body of work to suggest Pocognoli can adapt or oversee improvement. He achieved great success in Belgium, winning the title at Union Saint-Gilloise, before a brief spell at Monaco. The Scottish FA’s deep faith in this 39-year-old, amid all manner of waffle about metrics and analytics, was on the basis of just over 100 games as a manager. It remains probable that the association erred in not sourcing a coach with dugout experience at a country of similar scale to Scotland. This always had the whiff of trying to be too smart by half.
The best Scotland sides are unapologetically horrible to play against, physical, energetic and direct. Shortcomings in skill are offset by attitude. Pocognoli’s version is the opposite on all fronts, ponderous and timid. The Tartan Army, hardly a ferociously demanding lot, have failed to demonstrate any excitement about Pocognoli.
This counts as no ode to Clarke. After seven years, change was required. It was the turn taken by the Scottish FA in implementing a new strategy that looks increasingly dubious.
Footballers are typically selfish beings. For now it suits the Scotland squad – and is fair – to state Pocognoli requires time and that they are behind him. Not only did the body language amid the unravelling in St Gallen suggest otherwise, those players are likely to adopt a different position if focus turns towards them. Scotland’s contingent is heavy on influential, experienced players.
There is no sense of the Scottish FA dispensing with Pocognoli at this point. Not only would such a move be premature, it would deliver an admission of failure that those running the governing body are never keen on providing. They enjoy the trappings and profile provided by the national team without anything like the adjacent accountability. They are assisted in this context by domestic football obsession within the country. There will be grumblings about Pocognoli for a brief period this week before the theme is placed into cold storage.
Next month’s Uefa 2028 qualifying draw, where Scotland will appear from pot three, carries intrigue and danger for Pocognoli. The assumption that Scotland will feature in the tournament is undermined by performances; England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland are co-hosting and a maximum of two spots are open for any of those nations who do not qualify. Not playing in a competition where games will be staged in Glasgow would count as a humiliation for the Scottish FA.
If Scotland face competitive games rather than friendlies in March, which will be determined after the draw, Pocognoli needs stark improvement. Without it, his paymasters would then have a decision to make while looking to keep Euro 2028 dreams alive. The situation is already that acute.
Pocognoli was not part of the Scotland party that landed in Glasgow from Zurich on Tuesday. His family have remained in Belgium. Alone with his thoughts on his journey home, Pocognoli must have pondered the harshness of his new environment. He has the sternest of challenges to douse legitimate background noise.

items.title: A clash to savour at Ffos Las on Wednesday
items.summary:
Old Park Star, Sober Glory and Baron Noir clash at Ffos Las

items.text:
Old Park Star, Sober Glory and Baron Noir clash at Ffos Las
Having been declared to clash at Cheltenham over the weekend, Old Park Star and Sober Glory both swerved commitments at Prestbury Park in favour of more suitable conditions in South Wales on Wednesday, and we are treated to a fascinating contest with Baron Noir also thrown into the mix.
Tuesday 17 November 2026 17:32, UK
Cheltenham's loss is Ffos Las' gain on Wednesday as old rivals Old Park Star, Sober Glory and Baron Noir are set to face-off on chase debut and At The Races' Declan Rix previewed the contest.
You always need a bit of luck in this game, no matter what your role or ability. While the elements have unfortunately conspired against those at Exeter so far this season, Ffos Las is the beneficiary of what they are calling The Welsh Arkle on Wednesday, live on Sky Sports Racing.
The race got a huge boost with the somewhat surprise addition of 2026 Supreme Novices' Hurdle winner Old Park Star, a high-profile non-runner on Cheltenham's Saturday card due to the ground being deemed too quick. His inclusion means we have a huge early season clash with an old foe in Sober Glory, last season's unlucky Supreme runner-up.
The inclusion of Old Park Star is no doubt bad luck for those connected to Sober Glory et al; after all, the Henderson-trained horse was meant to run last Saturday, but it's a huge stroke of luck for Ffos Las and indeed, Sky Sports Racing. Exciting early season clashes like this are incredibly rare for novice chasers in Britain - and in general given the monster that the Cheltenham Festival has morphed into - so it's understandable there is a bit of a buzz around the industry ahead of the five-runner Golwg Gwendraeth Beginners' Chase, due off at 13:18pm.
Ground and weather
As of 8.37am on Tuesday, on the back of 16mm since 6pm on Monday, the ground is officially Good (good to soft in places), but with significant rain due. According to the BHA site, tomorrow's forecast reads as, 'blustery with persistent rain, heavy at times throughout the day'. Hopefully it leads to beautiful soft ground which the horses will get through nicely.
The big guns
As the official ratings and betting suggests, Old Park Star (155; 4/6) and Sober Glory (153; 15/8) are the standouts and are set to renew their rivalry having served up a fantastic Cheltenham Festival curtain raiser in March, along with Mydaddypaddy back in third. At the line, the winning margins were 1½ lengths and a nose, with the also reopposing Baron Noir (146; 10/1), Wednesday's third favourite, a further 6 lengths back in fourth.
Wednesday's prices and a glance at the formbook in black and white could lead you down the garden path of just siding the unbeaten hurdler Old Park Star, but replaying the final flight of their Supreme clash is wise, given it had such a significant impact on the race.
Heading to the last in the Supreme, Sober Glory looked to have everything in trouble with a good 1½+ lengths lead before he put in an extra stride, hit the hurdle and landed steeply, losing critical momentum. It was a huge shame for his connections because up to that point he had jumped so well and looked the best horse in the race going to the last.
That mistake cost him dearly, along with many punters having been a huge gamble from 16/1 in the morning to an SP of 9/2. The Philip Hobbs & Johnson White yard clearly felt like they had their charge in great order, produced him beautifully on the day only for that famous last flight on the Old Course at Prestbury Park to scupper a dream start to the 2026 Festival.
His disappointing run 31 days later at Aintree is easily excused on the back of a long season after a huge Cheltenham run and now with his attentions turned to chasing, this former Irish point-to-point winner for Cormac Doyle rates an exciting prospect for the upcoming campaign for owners Brocade Racing.
Standing in his way again is fellow six-year-old Old Park Star, who, to be fair, didn't exactly ping the final flight in the Supreme himself, also putting in an extra stride which led to the son of Well Chosen landing awkwardly but crucially, not losing as much momentum as Sober Glory.
That saw him stay unbeaten in four hurdle starts, after wins at Kempton, Cheltenham and Haydock, showing good versatility in terms of the tracks he could handle along with also displaying tactical adaptability. Having jumped right in places on debut, his hurdling got better and slicker as the campaign progressed and he looked a straight-forward character throughout.
Having been put away after Cheltenham, Old Park Star's attentions now to turn chasing, a game he possesses the physical scope and athleticism for, although unlike Sober Glory he has no point-to-point background. While not ideal, it's possibly a good sign that Nicky Henderson was willing to pitch him into Grade 2 company at Cheltenham on chasing debut before the ground ruled him out.
A horse said to be big and weak last season, there could be much more to come from Old Park Star, his trainer's comments of 'he's still a shell of a horse' last year continually playing on my mind. If he was able to achieve what he did last season when weak, you cannot but be excited about him after another summer on his back.
Chasing to put manners on Baron Noir?
Baron Noir is certainly no no-hoper against Old Park Star and Sober Glory, with 7½ lengths and 6 lengths, respectively, to find with the leading pair, especially if he has settled down for a summer's break and/or fences curb his keen-going ways.
It's in his breeding to be highly-strung, being by Vadamos out of a Dylan Thomas mare, but he's a horse with plenty of ability and it was a clear sign of the belief his trainer Alan King had in him to run in a Supreme when only rated 130.
While essentially well-held at the line, the six-year-old shaped better than the distance beaten, not getting up the hill as well as his Wednesday rivals. With that in mind, the much flatter nature of Ffos Las shou

Huang’s statement, posted in full on X, reads as follows:
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and s
items.text:
In the first public statement since his resignation, Nvidia founder Jensen Huang signalled his willingness to return as CEO if the board decides it is in the company’s best interest.
Huang’s statement, posted in full on X, reads as follows:
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I’ve never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA. 
I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 
Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO. 
Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.
Jensen
Huang resigned after reports of multiple affairs, including with a direct report and another with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is suspected of working with Chinese intelligence services. Nvidia’s chip exports have faced intense scrutiny since the revelations, and Huang is scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1.
In Huang’s absence, Nvidia has formed a new executive committee to oversee export control compliance.
Still, many investors and employees associated with Nvidia have called for Huang to return as CEO, at least until an investigation can provide clearer evidence of guilt. An open letter circulated earlier this week attracted the signatures of more than 10,000 current and former Nvidia employees, as well as prominent tech figures like Elon Musk, Amjad Masad, and Travis Kalanick.
“We are concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process,” the letter reads. “If the Board believes his continued absence is necessary, provide a specific, evidence-based explanation of why it serves NVIDIA’s best interests.”
Still, many see such a return as unlikely. On Monday, an unnamed source on Nvidia’s board told the Washington Post there were no plans to reinstate Huang. There’s also significant resistance to the idea in Congress, where Huang still faces significant questions about his role in chip exports to China-linked firms.
Reached by Politico, one senator called Huang’s reinstatement “one of the worst ideas I’ve heard today.”

items.title: Daydream’s new AI agent acts as your personal stylist — and can shop for you, too
items.summary:
Can an AI agent serve as your personal stylist? That’s what e-commerce veteran Julie Bornstein’s fashion startup, Daydream, aims to find out.
On Tuesday, the company launched “Daydream Agent,” an AI agent that is described as a personal stylist that can help you plan a look, virtually try on clothes
items.text:
Can an AI agent serve as your personal stylist? That’s what e-commerce veteran Julie Bornstein’s fashion startup, Daydream, aims to find out.
On Tuesday, the company launched “Daydream Agent,” an AI agent that is described as a personal stylist that can help you plan a look, virtually try on clothes, surface relevant pieces based on your taste, and more.
The idea, the company explains, is to put a personal stylist in everyone’s pocket. This application of AI could be promising, given that early adopters of consumer AI agents like Meta’s Muse have found that online shopping is a key use case.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently noted that shopping was a top activity for Muse’s over 10 million users, for instance, and that 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily.
In Daydream’s case, the fashion startup has been focused on using AI to deliver personalized shopping results to its users. Its new AI agent builds on its earlier work with an AI chatbot that could help users find outfits and make suggestions, but not complete purchases.
Now, the company says its Daydream Agent expands on that experience by remembering each shopper’s own personal style, fit preferences, and budget to refine its recommendations. Shoppers can also upload a photo to have the agent reuse that image to virtually try on any item they’ve saved. When they find something they like, the agent can complete a purchase through a one-click checkout process.
The agent can also handle other fashion-related tasks, like keeping an eye on when items go on sale, when brands have a new drop, providing weekly updates or spotting new fashion trends.
Also, instead of leaving items in their cart, shoppers can save pieces they’re interested in to a persistent “clothing rack” so they can compare options and think about their purchases before deciding what to buy. Shoppers can also connect their own closet and their calendar to the agent, helping them to build outfits around what they already own and plan what to wear for upcoming events.
The tech works by pulling real-time pricing and availability information from its catalog of over 10,000 brands, then combines that with its fashion-focused artificial intelligence.
However, considering that fashion is more of an art than a science, the company says it’s keeping humans in the loop. To do so, this month it brought on its first Stylist in Residence, Francesca Salih, an international fashion stylist and the founder of StyleGrid. Salih provides the startup with styling content that helps shape how the agent pulls together outfits and offers advice.
Bornstein, formerly Stitch Fix’s COO and the founder of The Yes (exited to Pinterest in 2022), started Daydream in 2023 as an AI search engine. The company, backed by $50 million in funding from Forerunner Ventures, Index Ventures, GV, and True Ventures, says more than 2 million shoppers have used Daydream to discover apparel and accessories since its June 2025 launch.

items.summary:
Arsenal transfer news: David Raya, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie close to finalising new contracts
David Raya and Jurrien Timber were about to enter the last 18 months of their Arsenal contracts; both players have rubberstamped their statuses as the best players in their positions in Europe; Pie
items.text:
Arsenal transfer news: David Raya, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie close to finalising new contracts
David Raya and Jurrien Timber were about to enter the last 18 months of their Arsenal contracts; both players have rubberstamped their statuses as the best players in their positions in Europe; Piero Hincapie only joined Arsenal on a permanent basis last summer
Tuesday 17 November 2026 16:53, UK
Arsenal are close to finalising new deals with David Raya, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie.
Sky Sports News reported on Monday that midfielder Declan Rice has verbally agreed a new contract and champions Arsenal are set to also tie down Raya, Timber and Hincapie.
Raya's current deal expires in 2028 but he is on the verge of signing an extension after establishing himself as one of the world's best goalkeepers since joining Arsenal, initially on loan from Brentford, in 2023.
- Transfer Centre LIVE! | Arsenal news & transfers🔴⚪
- Arsenal fixtures & scores | FREE Arsenal highlights▶️
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
Defender Timber joined Arsenal from Ajax in the same summer as Raya and his current contract is due to expire in 2028.
Speaking about reports he had agreed a new Arsenal deal, following the Netherlands 5-0 Nations League defeat against Germany on Monday, Timber told ESPN Netherlands: "Those are good reports. They are definitely on the right track! It will all work out, yes.
"If I extend, hopefully a few years will be added. You know better than I do. I feel at home here, I'm enjoying myself. Quinten [Timber - his twin brother at Crystal Palace] is in London now too, so we are doing well.
"I think we will definitely still be competing for trophies in the coming years. The club is happy with me as well, so that is good too. It all looks good."
Defender Hincapie - an initial loan signing from Bayer Leverkusen in 2025 - is also in talks over an extension with Arsenal confident he too will commit his long-term future to the club.
Arsenal on a contract roll - who else could get new deals?
Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:
Arsenal are going through a major contract renewal surge at the moment. Mikel Arteta has one of the best squads in Europe and - after the Arsenal manager committed to new terms earlier this year - he wants to keep it that way.
Other Arsenal players to commit to new contracts in the last 18 months include Bukayo Saka, Gabriel and William Saliba - while the long-term futures of high-profile youngsters such as Ethan Nwaneri, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Max Dowman have been secured.
In Timber, Raya and Declan Rice, Arsenal have ended any speculation about players moving towards the final year of their contract. The days of the early 2010s where Arsenal were sweating over the long-term futures of their major stars is clearly over.
But there are a still a handful of players who still have their futures hanging in the balance. The most pressing is captain Martin Odegaard, who has become a key player again after an injury-hit campaign last term.
The Norwegian midfielder, whose contract expires in 2028, has publicly revealed his desire to stay, but will a deal be struck before more questions and doubts start coming?
Another player entering the last 18 months of his contract is Kai Havertz - who again has had doubters and injury issues in recent years. With Arsenal's attack a clear area that needs to be improved, does one of Arteta's highest-paid players get another bump?
Ben White is another player whose contract expires in 2028, though the club have the option of an extra year extension on his deal. With Jurrien Timber, Ezri Konsa and Cristhian Mosquera also available for Arsenal in his position - a decision on his long-term future will also need to come soon.
The same contract expiry date also applies for Mikel Merino, who is struggling for regular minutes in a stacked Arsenal midfield that includes Lewis-Skelly, Bruno Guimaraes and Martin Zubimendi, who looks set to stay and fight for his place.
When Arsenal don't see a long-term vision for a player, they make it fairly clear when they let them go into the final year of their contracts. Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Jesus found that out, despite all three playing plenty of minutes across the season.
So what do Arsenal do with Odegaard, Havertz, White and Merino?

items.title: The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed
items.summary:
The Justice and Commerce Departments said that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company intertwined with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after reporting suggested an investigation had been halted last year.
The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed
The an
items.text:
The Justice and Commerce Departments said that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company intertwined with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after reporting suggested an investigation had been halted last year.
The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed
The announcement comes a week after revelations that Nvidia founder Jensen Huang was romantically linked to a leader at Megaspeed.
“While we don’t typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting,” the departments said in a statement issued Monday evening. The departments acknowledged there’s been “significant public attention” on Megaspeed.
Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO last week after reports he had an affair with former Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, who Megaspeed says left the company in August 2025. The scandal has raised questions about national security, and sparked scrutiny of Nvidia’s handling of exports of its chips to China and Megaspeed’s possible role in moving along Nvidia’s chips.
Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed “came to a sudden halt” late last year after its investigators received an email from Nvidia’s general counsel, claiming Commerce Department official Jeffrey Kessler gave Nvidia permission to reach out. The case was then “quickly” handed over to the DOJ, according to the Times.
The announcement today says the DOJ took the “lead role” in the investigation last year:
After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion, the Department of Commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations. In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed. In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list. Based on the Department of Commerce’s investigation, agents from the Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, conducted an on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed CEO Alice Huang.
Following this enforcement action, the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed.
The statement doesn’t go into detail about the current status of the case, but it says the DOJ and Commerce Department “will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred.”

items.text:
Senegal become first side to book Afcon 2027 spot
- Published
Senegal became the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) after Mozambique secured a 1-0 win away against Ethiopia.
That result means the Teranga Lions, who beat Sudan 4-2 on Monday, are guaranteed a top-two finish in Group J with two rounds of fixtures to play.
Eight more sides, including Morocco, Cameroon and Ivory Coast, could join Patrick Vieira's side in booking a spot at next year's finals as the fourth round of fixtures culminates on Tuesday.
Egypt could have qualified with an away win over Malawi but were held to a goalless draw after an inspired second-half showing from Flames goalkeeper George Chikooka.
After Mohamed Salah had hit the outside of the post from a tight angle, Chikooka denied Trezeguet and Haissem Hassan before also making fine stops from Mohamed Hany and Ibrahim Adel in stoppage time in Lilongwe.
The Pharaohs are now two points behind Angola in Group B after Miro's first-half effort secured a 1-0 victory for the Palancas Negras in South Sudan.
Meanwhile, Nigeria's hopes of progressing suffered another blow as the Super Eagles failed to beat tournament co-hosts Tanzania.
With the East Africans already assured of a spot at the finals, Nigeria are competing with Guinea-Bissau for just one qualification spot available in Group L.
A 0-0 draw in Zanzibar means the three-time continental champions could find themselves three points behind Guinea-Bissau if the Djurtus win away against Madagascar later in the day (16:00 GMT).
Elsewhere, Lesotho recorded a surprise 2-1 win over Gabon in Group A, leaving Morocco needing just a point from their match against Niger to go through.
The final two rounds of qualifiers will be held in March next year, with Afcon 2027 scheduled to be held in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from 19 June to 17 July.

items.title: Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO
items.summary:
Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO last week, would be willing to return as CEO if the company’s board of directors wanted it, he said in a statement reported on by The Wall Street Journal.
Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO
‘I would be honored to answer these calls and r
items.text:
Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO last week, would be willing to return as CEO if the company’s board of directors wanted it, he said in a statement reported on by The Wall Street Journal.
Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO
‘I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,’ Huang said.
“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”
Huang resigned on Thursday following reports of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy and a direct report. CFO Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO.
“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” Huang said. “I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.”
More than 193,000 people, including CEOs like Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, have signed a letter to “bring Jensen back.” President Trump has also been supportive of Huang returning as CEO, saying yesterday that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea.” (Trump had earlier tossed out former Apple CEO Tim Cook as a potential replacement.) On Monday, Nvidia’s board reportedly was “not considering” having Huang return, and today, CNN reported that the board is “not considering reinstating Huang.”
Nvidia didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.
Here is Huang’s full statement:
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I’ve never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.
I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.
Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.
Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.
Jensen
Update, November 17th: CNN reports that Nvidia’s board is not considering reinstating Huang.

items.title: South Africa head coach Erasmus banned for six matches
items.summary:
South Africa head coach Erasmus banned for six matches
- Published
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has been banned for six matches by World Rugby over comments he made about match officials in his side's Nations Championship defeat by France last week.
Speaking at a news conference conference
items.text:
South Africa head coach Erasmus banned for six matches
- Published
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has been banned for six matches by World Rugby over comments he made about match officials in his side's Nations Championship defeat by France last week.
Speaking at a news conference conference in Dublin on Monday before the Springboks' match with Ireland, Erasmus questioned what he perceived as double standards in officiating to the point where he asked: "is that not match-fixing?".
The two-time Rugby World Cup-winning coach was referencing the implementation of new rules surrounding hip-drop and knee-drop tackles, and felt the laws were not being applied correctly.
It comes after Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast became the first player to be cited for a hip-drop tackle in Ireland's win over Fiji on Saturday, which was not penalised in-play by referee Angus Gardner and television match official [TMO] Mike Adamson.
World Rugby said an independent panel determined that Erasmus' comments "suggest that match officials acted with bias/prejudice or deliberately influenced the outcome of a match".
In response, South Africa Rugby said it has requested a full misconduct hearing and an opportunity for Erasmus to "contextualise his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives".
It is the third time Erasmus has been sanctioned by World Rugby over his comments about match officials.
When he was South Africa's director of rugby, he was suspended for two months by World Rugby after he posted an hour-long video criticising the refereeing in the Springboks' opening Test defeat by the British and Irish Lions in 2021.
World Rugby found the video contained "multiple abusive and insulting comments and attacks on the officials".
In 2022, he received a two-match ban for a series of tweets criticising officials in a defeat by France.
Erasmus' latest ban has been imposed under World Rugby's match official abuse sanction process, which was introduced by the governing body in July.
If the suspension is upheld, Erasmus will miss Saturday's game with Ireland in Dublin (16:40 GMT), next week's finals weekend fixture at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium and the start of his side's Rugby Championship campaign next summer.
- 'Is that not match-fixing?' - Erasmus questions officiating 
  - Published17 hours ago
- Nations Championship final round - who needs what? 
  - Published23 hours ago
- Prendergast cited and could miss South Africa game 
  - Published1 day ago
Erasmus said that 17 hip-drop or knee-drop tackles had been missed in South Africa's 21-19 defeat in France by match officials. Andrea Piardi was the referee for the Stade de France fixture, while Matteo Liperini was the TMO.
Erasmus added that if TMOs were not intervening for reviews to limit the number of interruptions during a match then it was "manipulation", before he added that his comments were "not an accusation".
"I'm saying if he didn't see it, it must be a technology problem. If he saw it and decided not to act on it, is that not match-fixing?" Erasmus added.
"If the TMO didn't see it, maybe then technology must be better. If he saw it and he ignored it, what does that boil down to? Manipulation of the game or the result or injured players getting injured.
"So all I'm asking, don't take TMOs out and discourage them to get involved. Then the wrong team will win and players will get injured. That's all I'm saying."
'Unacceptable attack on credibility and competence of match officials'
In a statement on Tuesday, World Rugby said an independent panel determined that Erasmus' comments had met "the threshold for serious misconduct".
World Rugby confirmed the ban will stop Erasmus having any match day involvement for six matches, which includes coaching, direct or indirect contact with the team management or players on match days, entering the stadium, coaches' box, playing enclosure or technical area.
"The panel determined that the comments suggest that match officials acted with bias/prejudice or deliberately influenced the outcome of a match, and when the conduct is considered as a whole a reasonable person would conclude that the conduct constituted an unacceptable attack on the credibility and competence of the match officials," its statement said.
"In respect to the sanction, the panel determined that the conduct clearly amounts to disrespecting the authority of the match officials by impugning their integrity.
"Therefore, the panel reviewed a number of elements of the commentary including the timing and reach of the statements, combined with the allegations of bias or bad faith, and found that the comments attracted a six-match automatic suspension."
World Rugby added that "respect is fundamental to rugby, and match officials are central to the sport".
"Protecting their wellbeing and integrity, and their right to perform without abuse or intimidation, is a responsibility World Rugby and unions take seriously," their statement added.
"Coaches, players, unions and everyone in the game must uphold these standards.
"Robust, respectful debate is natural, but teams have access to well-established and supported channels and protocols for raising officiating matters before and after matches. Challenging a decision is not the same as questioning an official's integrity or making comments that expose them to personal abuse."
In the same news conference, which lasted more than half an hour at the Springboks' team hotel, Erasmus also questioned what he felt were double standards in terms of sanctions.
The outcome of the citing has yet to be released, but he predicted that Prendergast will be available to play against South Africa due to a "technicality", and also questioned the decision not to ban Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong for an alleged groin grab while playing for Leinster ahead of the November Tests.
Last year, South Africa prop Jan-Hendrik Wessels was handed a nine-match ban

items.title: Wayne Rooney says he contemplated taking own life during playing career
items.summary: Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated taking his own life. The former England striker said that, even as he flourished on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it, despite being newly married and a dad to his eldest child
items.text:
Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated taking his own life. The former England striker said that, even as he flourished on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it, despite being newly married and a dad to his eldest child, Kai.
He said he would spend two days at a time drinking at home and, he told the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, at his lowest point considered taking his own life. “I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” Rooney said. “Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.
“I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to be see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops. I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else [I] really struggled with it.”
Rooney, United’s record goalscorer, said the issues he faced occurred at the height of his career. “You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,” he said. “Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man if you like for doing that.
“I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I’ve just had a young son, I’ve just been married. It should be the happiest point in my life and it wasn’t. It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.”
Rooney, who is currently featuring on the ITV reality programme I’m a Celebrity … Get Me Out of Here!, credits his wife, Coleen, with helping him turn the tide. “Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it.”

As well as England,
items.text:
FA wants to host Nations League finals in England
- Published
England could host the Nations League finals this season after Football Association officials registered their interest.
The semi-final and finals of the competition, due to take place in June, are held in one country.
As well as England, it is understood that Spain and France have also contacted Uefa to register their interest in hosting the final four games, including the bronze medal match, which will run between 9-13 June.
The FA, it is understood, is still discussing potential venues with some doubt over whether Wembley would be available. The only publicly announced Wembley events in June are two concerts by singer Sam Fender, although these are for after the Nations League.
Since the tournament began in 2019, England have never held the finals, with Portugal, Italy, Netherlands and Germany the hosts to date.
Generally, only nations who reach the last four of the Nations League are considered to host the latter stages.
Thomas Tuchel's team will be seeded in Friday's draw for the quarter-finals following their euphoric 3-2 victory over Spain in Madrid, which secured top place in the group.
They could face Belgium, Netherlands, Denmark or Norway in March in the next round before June's finals.
If the FA's bid is successful, it will provide the governing body with an opportunity to host a mini-tournament before Euro 2028, which will be held in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

items.text:
ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev books place in semi-finals after brushing aside Ben Shelton; Arthur Fils beats Rafael Jodar
Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton in straight sets to book his place in the knockout stages of the ATP Finals; Rafael Jodar will not progress past the groups after he suffered defeat to Arthur Fils; watch the ATP Nitto Finals live on Sky Sports Tennis
Tuesday 17 November 2026 22:42, UK
Alexander Zverev booked his spot in the knockout stages of the ATP Finals after sealing a ruthless 6-2 7-6 (7-4) victory over Ben Shelton in Turin on Tuesday night, in a rematch of this year's US Open final.
His victory means debutant Rafael Jodar will not advance to the semi-finals after the Spaniard suffered defeat to Zverev in their opening match of the tournament, before being bested 4-6 6-2 6-2 by Arthur Fils earlier in the day.
Zverev, whose service game was impeccable against Shelton, will jump to the top of the John McEnroe Group standings, having not dropped a set so far during the tournament, as he swept away the American to bring up a flawless 7-0 winning record against the 24-year-old.
